preamble: The dental affricate [ts] palatalizes to the alveolo-palatal [tɕ] before high front vowels and [j]. In Mandarin and Northern Wu, Middle Chinese ts- in this position merged with palatalized velars into a single alveolo-palatal series (the jiān–tuán merger), while Cantonese and Hakka keep [ts]. Seoul Korean palatalized Middle Korean apical ㅈ [ts] to [tɕ]; northwestern (Pyongyang) speech still keeps [ts].

examples.note: Cantonese zing1 [tsɪŋ⁵⁵] keeps the dental affricate.
The same outcome is listed for Hangzhou, Ningbo and Shaoxing Wu.
Middle Korean ㅈ was apical; Seoul ㅈ is [tɕ], while Pyongyang speech typically keeps [ts].

sources: Norman, J. (1988). Chinese. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521296533
